quarterly_data.quarter: Apple press release: Apple introduces M6 and M5 Ultra for a big leap in (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Apple debuted M6 (in the new Mac mini) and M5 Ultra (in the new Mac Studio) on August 25, 2026. M6 is Apple's first 2-nanometer chip; Sri Santhanam, Apple's vice president of Silicon Engineering Group: 'Built using the cutting-edge 2 nm process, M6 combines a new CPU complex, two additional CPU and GPU cores, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and more unified memory bandwidth'. M6 has a 12-core CPU (2 super cores, 4 performance cores, 6 efficiency cores; up to 1.2x faster multithreaded than M5), a 12-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in each core (a nearly 30 percent increase in peak GPU compute for AI versus M5), a Dual 16-core Neural Engine (up to 2x the peak compute over previous generations), up to 32GB of unified memory and up to 170GB/s of bandwidth (a 10 percent increase over M5). M5 Ultra is Apple's first quad-die architecture: UltraFusion connects two dual-die M5 Max chips, increasing inter-die bandwidth to over 4.4TB/s and connection density by over 6x, so the four dies behave as a single unified processor. M5 Ultra has an up-to-36-core CPU (12 super cores and 24 performance cores), an up-to-80-core GPU with Neural Accelerators (up to 4.5x the peak GPU compute for AI of M3 Ultra), a 32-core Neural Engine, and up to 512GB of unified memory at 1.2TB/s (50 percent higher than M3 Ultra). Apple calls M5 Ultra its most powerful chip ever (company claim). The release does not name the foundry.
quarterly_data.figure: M6: first 2 nm Apple chip, 12-core CPU / 12-core GPU, up to 170GB/s; M5 Ultra: quad-die via UltraFusion, inter-die bandwidth over 4.4TB/s, connection density over 6x, up to 512GB at 1.2TB/s
